nodes.title: Deliver a locally runnable Safari build target
nodes.description:
## Outcome Trace
- SAFARI-BUILD: A developer enters through `npm run debug -- --safari`, builds the shared Dark Reader sources as a Safari-specific MV2 extension directory, finds it again at `build/debug/safari`, receives a failing build with no partial success claim when generation or validation fails, proves it with automated build and manifest evidence, is implemented first by `safari-web-extension-artifact`, reaches its earliest seam at `SAFARI-EXTENSION-DIR`, and closes only at `safari-runtime-acceptance`.
- SAFARI-PACKAGE: A macOS developer enters through the documented `xcrun safari-web-extension-packager` command, packages the current Safari extension directory as a development-only containing app, finds the generated project under `build/safari-app`, regenerates only that ignored directory after packaging corruption, proves it with packager and Xcode project evidence, is implemented first by `safari-macos-package`, reaches its earliest seam at `SAFARI-MACOS-PACKAGE`, and closes only at `safari-runtime-acceptance`.
- SAFARI-LOCAL-RUN: A macOS Safari user enters through Safari Extensions settings after locally signing and running the containing app, observes Dark Reader darken and toggle a permitted light webpage, finds retained settings after restarting Safari, sees safe inaccessible-page behavior when permission is denied, proves it with manual Safari behavior evidence, is implemented by `safari-runtime-acceptance`, reaches its earliest seam at `SAFARI-RUN-EVIDENCE`, and closes at that same terminal gate.
- EXISTING-TARGETS-UNCHANGED: A Dark Reader developer enters through the existing default and explicit browser build commands, receives the same pre-Safari target selection and valid existing artifacts, finds them at their established build paths, treats any changed target selection or failed regression check as blocking, proves it with automated regression evidence, is implemented first by `safari-web-extension-artifact`, reaches its earliest seam at `SAFARI-EXTENSION-DIR`, and closes only at `safari-runtime-acceptance`.

## Success Criteria
- All four outcomes have PASS evidence from their named final gate; FAIL, BLOCKED, UNTESTED, SKIPPED, or stale evidence leaves the epic open.
- The Safari target is opt-in, MV2, nonpersistent, free of unsupported `fontSettings`, and packaged without native messaging or committed Xcode output.
- Apple's packager and the generated Xcode project consume the current `build/debug/safari` artifact without copied extension resources.
- Safari behavior proves darkening, site toggling, persistence across restart, and safe permission denial on the current supported local toolchain.
- Existing browser builds, unit tests, and lint remain passing.

nodes.title: Build an opt-in Safari web extension artifact
nodes.description:
## Context
- Product contract: User-authorized omission recorded in the approved spec; the original request and approved design govern scope.
- Spec: `docs/specs/2026-07-23-safari-build-target-design.md`, approved 2026-07-23.
- Outcome IDs: SAFARI-BUILD, EXISTING-TARGETS-UNCHANGED.
- External ref: Apple compatibility and background lifecycle documentation linked from the approved spec.
- Why this slice exists: It is the earliest end-to-end seam that turns shared Dark Reader sources into a Safari-specific artifact that Apple's packager can consume.
- Complexity boundaries: parsing, protocol.
- Acceptance surface: One opt-in command produces a valid Safari extension directory and release archive without changing existing target selection.
- Constraints: Use the shared platform build pipeline; retain MV2; set a nonpersistent background page; do not add dependencies or modify `package.json` or `package-lock.json`.

## Outcome
- Actor / entry interface: A developer with repository dependencies installed runs `npm run debug -- --safari` or `npm run build -- --release --safari`.
- Observable result: The command succeeds only for the requested Safari target and reports ordinary build success.
- Durable result / find-again path: A complete extension is available at `build/debug/safari` or `build/release/safari`, with the release ZIP at `build/release/darkreader-safari.zip`.
- Denied/failure/recovery result: An invalid selection, missing source, manifest failure, or bundling failure exits nonzero; rerunning after correcting the source regenerates only the selected build output.

## Domain Contract
- Vocabulary: Safari target means the repository's Safari-specific web extension artifact, not the generated macOS containing app and not the separately distributed official Safari product.
- Ownership: The existing Node build pipeline owns generated extension resources; `src/manifest-safari.json` owns Safari manifest differences.
- Authority: Build flags select targets; user-agent spoofing and a reused Chrome artifact cannot select Safari behavior.
- Invariants: Safari remains opt-in; all existing compile-time browser flags are false for Safari; the manifest is MV2 and nonpersistent; required webpage access remains declared; `fontSettings`, native messaging, and unsupported debug-only permissions are absent.
- Transitions: Shared sources plus Safari selection become a disposable debug or release output; source changes replace generated output on the next build.
- Side-effect boundary: Writes are limited to existing generated `build/` paths; source manifests for other targets are not mutated.
- Counterexample: Renaming a Chrome output directory to `safari` fails this contract because it retains Chromium compile-time branches.

## Files
- Create: `src/manifest-safari.json` for the Safari MV2 manifest patch.
- Create: `tests/unit/config/safari-manifest.tests.ts` for the focused merged-manifest contract.
- Modify: `tasks/platform.js` to define the Safari platform identifier.
- Modify: `tasks/build.js` to parse explicit Safari selection while excluding Safari from the legacy default target set.
- Modify: `tasks/cli.js` to validate and document `--safari`.
- Modify: `tasks/bundle-html.js` to emit the MV2 background page for Safari.
- Modify: `tasks/bundle-manifest.js` to apply Safari-safe debug permission behavior.
- Modify: `tasks/zip.js` to emit Safari release output as ZIP rather than XPI.
- Test: `tests/unit/config/safari-manifest.tests.ts` merges the base and Safari manifests and asserts the Safari contract.

## Resources
- Exclusive resources: `build/debug/safari`, `build/release/safari`, `build/release/darkreader-safari.zip`.
- Capacity resources: One Node build process with the repository's normal memory allowance.

## Interfaces
- Produces: SAFARI-EXTENSION-DIR — `npm run debug -- --safari` produces a complete extension rooted at `build/debug/safari`; the release variant produces the corresponding release directory and ZIP.
- Consumes: None.
- Hard ordering constraints: None.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Automated build evidence PASS: `npm run debug -- --safari` exits zero and `build/debug/safari/manifest.json` references only files present in that directory.
- Manifest contract evidence PASS: `npm run test:unit -- --runInBand tests/unit/config/safari-manifest.tests.ts` proves MV2, `background.page` equal to `background/index.html`, `background.persistent` false, required host access present, and `fontSettings` absent.
- Release evidence PASS: `npm run build -- --release --safari` exits zero and produces `build/release/darkreader-safari.zip`.
- Selection evidence PASS: `node tasks/cli.js build --help` advertises `--safari`, while the no-target default set remains exactly Chrome MV2, Chrome MV3, Firefox MV2, and Thunderbird subject to the existing Plus availability rule.
- Regression evidence PASS: `npm test` and `npm run lint` exit zero; any FAIL, BLOCKED, UNTESTED, or SKIPPED result leaves SAFARI-BUILD and EXISTING-TARGETS-UNCHANGED open.

## Integration Checkpoint
Run `npm run debug -- --safari`, then parse `build/debug/safari/manifest.json` and verify every declared background, content-script, popup, icon, and locale path exists under that same artifact. This exercises the real interface consumed by Apple's packager.

## Implementation Notes
- RED: After repository setup with `npm install`, `npm run debug -- --safari` currently fails because `--safari` is not a valid target and no Safari platform or manifest exists. If dependencies are absent, install them first without accepting lockfile changes.
- GREEN boundary: Add the platform, selection, manifest, background HTML inclusion, Safari-safe permission rule, ZIP classification, and focused manifest test only; do not add a package script or native project.
- GREEN: Run the focused unit test, debug build, and release build until each passes with the specified artifact shape.
- Final verification: Run `npm test`, `npm run lint`, inspect CLI help/default selection, and retain command output as task evidence.

nodes.title: Package the Safari artifact as a local macOS app
nodes.description:
## Context
- Product contract: User-authorized omission recorded in the approved spec; the original request and approved design govern scope.
- Spec: `docs/specs/2026-07-23-safari-build-target-design.md`, approved 2026-07-23.
- Outcome IDs: SAFARI-PACKAGE.
- External ref: `https://developer.apple.com/documentation/safariservices/packaging-a-web-extension-for-safari` and the locally inspected `xcrun safari-web-extension-packager --help` from Xcode 26.5.
- Why this slice exists: A valid extension directory is not a persistent Safari installation; this slice exercises its first consumer by generating and inspecting the macOS containing app.
- Complexity boundaries: protocol, security.
- Acceptance surface: The documented Apple command converts the current Safari artifact into a development-only macOS Xcode project without copied resources or committed signing state.
- Constraints: macOS only; Swift wrapper; no `--copy-resources`; no `--force`; no native messaging; no App Store, notarization, iOS, or committed generated project.

## Outcome
- Actor / entry interface: A macOS developer follows `docs/safari.md` after producing `build/debug/safari`.
- Observable result: Apple's packager completes and the generated Xcode project exposes a macOS app target and Safari web extension target based on the current artifact.
- Durable result / find-again path: The disposable project is found under `build/safari-app` and continues to reference `build/debug/safari` for subsequent rebuilds.
- Denied/failure/recovery result: A missing or invalid artifact stops packaging; an existing wrapper is not overwritten; corruption is recovered by removing only `build/safari-app` and rerunning the documented command.

## Domain Contract
- Vocabulary: Containing app means Apple's generated local macOS wrapper; it is not maintained application source and grants no native capability.
- Ownership: Apple owns generated project structure; the repository owns the input artifact and runbook; the developer owns local signing selections.
- Authority: Xcode controls local signing and Safari controls extension enablement; no certificate, team, token, profile, or entitlement enters Git.
- Invariants: App name is `Dark Reader Development`; bundle identifier is `com.the-inconvenience-store.darkreader.development`; resources are referenced rather than copied; output remains ignored; native messaging is absent.
- Transitions: A passing SAFARI-EXTENSION-DIR becomes an ignored Xcode project; repeated web builds update the referenced artifact without project regeneration.
- Side-effect boundary: Packaging writes only under `build/safari-app` and may open Xcode only when the developer chooses; it does not modify source manifests.
- Counterexample: Committing the generated project or using the official Dark Reader bundle identity fails this contract.

## Files
- Create: `docs/safari.md` as the build, package, local-signing, enablement, update, warning-triage, and recovery runbook.
- Modify: `README.md` to link the opt-in Safari development runbook from the build documentation.
- Test: `docs/safari.md` by executing its build and packaging commands on the current macOS toolchain.

## Resources
- Exclusive resources: `build/safari-app`, local Xcode signing selections for `Dark Reader Development`.
- Capacity resources: One macOS Xcode and Safari web extension packager process.

## Interfaces
- Produces: SAFARI-MACOS-PACKAGE — the generated project under `build/safari-app` references SAFARI-EXTENSION-DIR and exposes the local macOS app and extension targets.
- Consumes: SAFARI-EXTENSION-DIR.
- Hard ordering constraints: None.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Packager evidence PASS: the exact documented `xcrun safari-web-extension-packager` command exits zero against `build/debug/safari` without `--copy-resources` or `--force`.
- Reference evidence PASS: a generated `.xcodeproj` exists below `build/safari-app`, and its project configuration references `build/debug/safari` rather than a copied resource tree.
- Xcode project evidence PASS: resolving the generated project with `find build/safari-app -name '*.xcodeproj' -print -quit` and passing it to `xcodebuild -list -project` reports the containing app and extension targets.
- Security evidence PASS: `git status --short` shows no generated Xcode or signing files, and the generated manifest/project adds no native messaging permission or credential material.
- Runbook evidence PASS: a fresh reader can follow `docs/safari.md` from build through Sign to Run Locally, Safari developer-mode and unsigned-extension enablement, rebuild, warning triage, and bounded wrapper regeneration; any critical packager warning or non-PASS item leaves SAFARI-PACKAGE open.

## Integration Checkpoint
Execute the runbook through Apple packaging, resolve the generated `.xcodeproj`, and run `xcodebuild -list -project` against it. Inspect the project reference to confirm that the first consumer uses the live `build/debug/safari` artifact.

## Implementation Notes
- RED: Before this slice, `test -d build/safari-app` fails and no repository runbook leads from SAFARI-EXTENSION-DIR to a macOS containing app.
- GREEN boundary: Add only the runbook and README link, then execute Apple's installed packager with the approved macOS-only Swift, development-name, and reference-resource options.
- GREEN: Confirm packager success, project discovery, target listing, live resource reference, ignored output, and absence of native messaging or credentials.
- Final verification: Repeat the runbook from a regenerated Safari artifact; retain packager warnings and Xcode target listing as task evidence.

nodes.title: Prove the packaged extension in Safari
nodes.description:
## Context
- Product contract: User-authorized omission recorded in the approved spec; the original request and approved design govern scope.
- Spec: `docs/specs/2026-07-23-safari-build-target-design.md`, approved 2026-07-23.
- Outcome IDs: SAFARI-BUILD, SAFARI-PACKAGE, SAFARI-LOCAL-RUN, EXISTING-TARGETS-UNCHANGED.
- External ref: `https://developer.apple.com/documentation/safariservices/running-your-safari-web-extension` and `https://developer.apple.com/documentation/safariservices/developing-a-safari-web-extension`.
- Why this slice exists: Build and packaging success cannot prove page injection, popup behavior, persistence, or safe permission denial in Safari; this is the terminal product-evidence gate.
- Complexity boundaries: evidence, security.
- Acceptance surface: One locally signed and enabled development extension completes the approved Safari journey and leaves all automated regression evidence passing.
- Constraints: Use Sign to Run Locally with Team None for both generated targets; enable Safari developer features and Allow Unsigned Extensions; use a non-sensitive light test page; do not broaden site permission beyond what the tester intentionally grants; do not commit generated or signing state.

## Outcome
- Actor / entry interface: A macOS developer locally signs and runs SAFARI-MACOS-PACKAGE, enables `Dark Reader Development` in Safari Extensions settings, and opens a permitted light webpage.
- Observable result: The popup opens, the page becomes dark, the per-site toggle works, and denied permission produces the existing safe inaccessible-page behavior instead of a crash.
- Durable result / find-again path: The extension remains listed after Safari restarts and the changed popup setting remains present when the extension is reopened.
- Denied/failure/recovery result: A denied page stays unmodified without background or popup failure; any missing extension, crash, lost setting, or failed regression evidence keeps all affected outcomes open and routes correction to the owning build or package seam.

## Domain Contract
- Vocabulary: Runtime acceptance means observed Safari extension behavior, not an Xcode build result or a temporarily loaded folder.
- Ownership: Safari owns enablement and website permission; Dark Reader owns popup, injection, toggle, and setting behavior; the developer owns the local test profile.
- Authority: Only the tester grants website access; the extension cannot bypass a denial.
- Invariants: The test uses the generated development identity, current referenced artifact, non-sensitive page, and no native bridge; existing browser regressions remain PASS.
- Transitions: Locally signed app becomes an enabled Safari extension; granted access permits darkening; denied access leaves the page unchanged; restart restores installed state and settings.
- Side-effect boundary: Test state is limited to the local Safari profile, development app, website permission, and Dark Reader settings.
- Counterexample: A successful `xcodebuild` with no observed page darkening does not satisfy SAFARI-LOCAL-RUN.

## Files
- Create: None; this is a validation-only terminal gate.
- Modify: None; corrections belong to the seam that fails its evidence.
- Test: None in source; execute the approved manual Safari journey and automated regression commands.

## Resources
- Exclusive resources: Local Safari development profile, `Dark Reader Development` app and extension identity.
- Capacity resources: One interactive macOS Safari session and one local Xcode run destination.

## Interfaces
- Produces: SAFARI-RUN-EVIDENCE — timestamped PASS evidence for local install, popup, darkening, site toggle, persistence, denial safety, and existing-target regressions on the current macOS/Safari/Xcode versions.
- Consumes: SAFARI-EXTENSION-DIR, SAFARI-MACOS-PACKAGE.
- Hard ordering constraints: None.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Installation evidence PASS: both generated targets use Sign to Run Locally with Team None, the app runs, Safari allows unsigned extensions for development, and `Dark Reader Development` can be enabled in Safari.
- Behavior evidence PASS: on a permitted light page the popup opens, darkening is visible, and toggling the current site off and on changes the page accordingly.
- Persistence evidence PASS: change one harmless popup setting, quit and reopen Safari, then confirm the extension remains listed and the setting is retained.
- Denial evidence PASS: deny access for a test site and confirm the page remains unmodified while the popup/background remain operable and communicate the inaccessible state through existing behavior.
- Final regression evidence PASS: rerun `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run debug -- --safari`, and one representative existing explicit target build; any FAIL, BLOCKED, UNTESTED, SKIPPED, or stale result leaves the corresponding outcomes and epic open.
- Repository evidence PASS: `git status --short` contains only authorized source changes and no generated Xcode, signing, credential, or `build/` artifacts.

## Integration Checkpoint
Run the locally signed containing app, enable its extension in Safari, grant access to a light test page, exercise popup darkening and toggling, restart Safari for persistence, then deny one site's access and verify safe behavior. Record the current macOS, Safari, and Xcode versions with the evidence.

## Implementation Notes
- RED: Before local signing and enablement, Safari does not expose a persistent `Dark Reader Development` extension journey and no runtime evidence exists.
- GREEN boundary: Make no source changes in this gate unless a failed criterion identifies an owning earlier seam; route corrections there and rerun their checks before repeating acceptance.
- GREEN: Complete installation, behavior, persistence, denial, regression, and clean-repository checks with fresh evidence.
- Final verification: Confirm every epic outcome has current PASS evidence; otherwise leave the task and epic open with the exact failing criterion.
